title: Cap. VI Arg. 13: sounder scholastics — willing to receive grace is from predestination
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the sounder Scholastics themselves, who are wont to attribute more than is equal to human choice, yet do not dare to recall the discrimination of elect and passed-by to the good and bad use of free choice in embracing or rejecting grace. Whence Thomas, Disputed Questions on Predestination, article 2: This very willing to receive grace is from Divine predestination. And Durandus, p. 250: Every good that is done by someone, or that helps him to the attainment of the supernatural end, whether by cause or by occasion, falls under the effect of predestination.
pass_b_english: Even the sounder scholastics, who usually credit free choice more than is due, dare not reduce the split between elect and passed-by to good or bad use of free choice in embracing or rejecting grace. So Aquinas (Disputed Questions on Predestination, art. 2): this very willing to receive grace is from divine predestination. And Durandus (p. 250): every good done by someone, or that helps him reach the supernatural end — whether as cause or occasion — falls under predestination's effect.
source_text: Quinetiam ipsi Scholastici saniores, qui plus aequo tribuere solent humano arbitrio, tamen non audent electorum et praeteritorum discrimen ad bonum et malum usum liberi arbitrii in gratia amplexanda vel repellenda revocare. Unde Thomas, Qu. disp. de praed. art. 2: Hoc ipsum velle accipere gratiam est ex praedestinatione Divina. Et Durandus, pag. 250: Omne bonum quod fit ab aliquo, vel quod juvat eum ad consecutionem finis supernaturalis, sive per causam, sive per occasionem, cadit sub effectu praedestinationis.
